costGuide.title: Lexus 2GR-FXS Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 2GR-FXS typically takes 12-16 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent Lexus hybrid specialist) - the V6 is tightly packaged and the hybrid system adds significant complexity .
paragraphs: What moves the price most for this engine is whether the replacement unit includes a new water pump (a known weak point) and whether the EGR cooler and coolant crossover pipes have been addressed. A reconditioned 2GR-FXS with documented cooling system refresh and decarbonised intake valves is well worth the premium - these are the key service items on this engine. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide for more detail.

failures.title: Lexus 2GR-FXS Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Water pump failure - seepage and bearing noise
items.whatHappens: The water pump on the 2GR-FXS is a known service item, just like its non-hybrid sibling. The seals degrade over time, leading to a slow coolant seepage from the pump weep hole. If ignored, the pump bearing can fail, causing a sudden loss of coolant and potential overheating. Symptoms include a sweet coolant smell, visible pink/red residue around the pump, and a whirring noise from the front of the engine at idle. On the hybrid system, overheating is particularly serious as it can affect the inverter and battery cooling.
items.repairVsReplace: Water pump replacement is a standalone job (£500-£900 parts and labour at an indie). It does not write off the engine. However, if the engine has overheated due to pump failure, the aluminium heads can warp - at which point a reconditioned replacement engine becomes the sensible route.

items.title: Coolant crossover pipe leaks - plastic pipe failure
items.whatHappens: The 2GR-FXS uses a plastic coolant crossover pipe at the front of the engine (a design shared with the 2GR-FSE). Over time, the plastic can become brittle and crack, leading to coolant loss. This is a well-documented issue on the 2GR family, and on the hybrid, coolant loss can also affect the inverter cooling system.
items.repairVsReplace: The crossover pipe is a standalone component (£300-£600 parts and labour). Replacement with an updated design is recommended if the engine is being reconditioned. It does not write off the engine, but ignoring a leak can lead to overheating.

items.title: EGR cooler clogging - reduced efficiency and potential overheating
items.whatHappens: Like many modern direct-injection engines, the 2GR-FXS's EGR cooler can become clogged with soot and carbon over time. A partially blocked cooler reduces EGR flow, which can increase combustion temperatures and, in extreme cases, lead to detonation or overheating. On the hybrid V6, this can also affect fuel economy and emissions performance.
items.repairVsReplace: The EGR cooler can be cleaned or replaced as a standalone job (£400-£800). This is a service item, not a catastrophic failure.

items.title: Carbon buildup on intake valves - D-4S side effect (less severe than 2GR-FSE)
items.whatHappens: The 2GR-FXS uses D-4S dual-injection (port + direct) on the Atkinson cycle, which provides some fuel washing over the intake valves. As a result, carbon buildup is less severe than on the 2GR-FSE, but it still occurs over time, particularly on vehicles used primarily for short trips. Symptoms include rough idle, hesitation under load, and reduced fuel economy.
items.repairVsReplace: Walnut-shell blasting of the intake valves (£400-£800) restores performance. This is a service item, not a failure.

failures.goodYearsLine: The 2GR-FXS is a mature, well-developed engine. 2018+ models have revised water pump and crossover pipe components. Overall, this is one of the most durable hybrid V6s on the market - expect 200,000+ miles with routine maintenance.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 2GR-FXS
variants.intro: The 2GR-FXS is Lexus's 3.5-litre Atkinson-cycle V6 hybrid engine, fitted to the RX450h and GS450h. The code is physically stamped on the engine block - typically on the front side of the block, just below the cylinder head on the driver's side (UK passenger side), or on a machined pad near the bellhousing. Commonly confused with: - 2GR-FSE - the 3.5‑litre D-4S V6 used in non‑hybrid IS350 and GS350. The FSE runs the Otto cycle and is not a hybrid engine - it has different pistons, cam profiles, and no electric motor integration. Not interchangeable. - 2GR-FXE - the 3.5‑litre Atkinson‑cycle hybrid V6 used in the earlier RX450h (AL10 pre‑2015) and Toyota Sienna Hybrid. The FXE is an older design with slightly lower output and different ECU calibration - not a swap for the FXS without significant rework. - 2GR-FKS - the 2.5‑litre, sorry, wait - the 2GR-FKS is actually a different engine, but the 2GR-FKS doesn't exist - the newer 3.5L in the Tundra/Highlander is 2GR-FKS? Actually, the 2GR-FKS is a 3.5L V6 but with different tuning - it's in the Toyota Highlander and Sienna (non-hybrid), and shares some architecture but not the Atkinson cycle or hybrid integration. Not a swap.

relatives.description: the 3.5‑litre Atkinson‑cycle V6 hybrid engine used in the earlier Lexus RX450h (AL10 pre‑2015) and Toyota Sienna Hybrid. The FXS is a significant evolution with higher output, improved thermal efficiency, and better refinement - but shares the same fundamental architecture. Not a straight swap without ECU and hybrid system adjustments.

the 2.4‑litre turbocharged hybrid engine introduced in newer Lexus models (RX350h, NX350h) as a replacement for the 3.5‑litre V6 hybrid. It delivers comparable power with significantly better fuel economy, but a very different character - the V6 is smoother and more refined, the turbo four more responsive in the mid‑range. Not a swap option.

the 3.5‑litre D-4S V6 used in the Toyota Highlander, Sienna, and some Lexus models (non‑hybrid). It shares the same block but runs the Otto cycle - not a hybrid engine. Not interchangeable with the FXS.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 2GR-FXS - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used 2GR‑FXS can be a cost‑effective choice for older RX450h/GS450h values, provided the donor has documented service history. The key checks are: (1) has the water pump been replaced? (2) have the coolant crossover pipes been inspected? A used unit with a fresh water pump and crossover pipes - and less than 80,000 miles - offers excellent value. Link once: [used engines service]

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A properly reconditioned 2GR‑FXS should include a new water pump, new coolant crossover pipes (updated design), a cleaned EGR cooler, a professional decarbonisation of the intake valves (walnut blasting), and a full top‑end gasket set. The timing chain and guides are rarely an issue on this engine. This is the sweet spot for RX450h and GS450h owners - you get a like‑new V6 hybrid with the key weak points addressed, at a fraction of the cost of a new unit from Lexus. Reconditioned units typically come with a 12-24 month warranty. Link once: [reconditioned engines service]

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is only justified for low‑mileage, cherished vehicles (e.g. a clean‑car RX450h with low chassis miles). A quality rebuild will include bottom‑end bearings, piston rings, valve guides, seals, and a full timing system refresh. This is the most expensive option but offers the closest thing to a new engine. Link once: [rebuilt engines service]

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All options above can be supplied and fitted through our network of vetted UK Lexus specialists. Each quote includes warranty details and delivery options. Link once: [supply and fit service]
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The 2GR‑FXS sits in high‑value vehicles - RX450h (£12,000-£35,000) and GS450h (£8,000-£20,000). A reconditioned engine at £3,500-£5,500 represents roughly 15-40% of the car's value - which is justifiable for a premium Lexus hybrid that, once refreshed, will outlast the chassis. For a higher‑mileage GS450h worth under £8,000, a used engine with a solid warranty is often the most sensible financial choice. Always factor in the condition of the hybrid battery, transmission, and suspension before committing to an expensive reconditioned engine.

items.answer: Given the high value of 2GR‑FXS host vehicles (RX450h, GS450h), a reconditioned unit is the sweet spot for most owners - it comes with a new water pump, updated coolant crossover pipes, cleaned EGR cooler, decarbonised intake valves, and a 12‑24 month warranty. Used units can be cost‑effective for higher‑mileage examples, but always budget for preventative cooling system work (new water pump and crossover pipes) before fitting. items.answer: The engine code is stamped on the block (typically on the front side, just below the cylinder head on the driver's side) and is also on your V5C under “Engine number”. Alternatively, enter your registration above and we'll confirm your exact fitment. Check your engine via registration
bullets: Don't confuse it with the 2GR‑FSE (non‑hybrid, Otto‑cycle) or the 2GR‑FXE (older hybrid) - they are not interchangeable.
If your RX or GS is badged "450h" with a 3.5‑litre V6 hybrid, it's almost certainly the 2GR‑FXS.

items.question: How long does a 2GR‑FXS engine typically last?
items.answer: With proper maintenance, the 2GR‑FXS is expected to exceed 200,000 miles. The engine is chain‑driven, so no timing belt replacement is needed. Regular oil changes (every 10,000 miles or 12 months) and coolant flushes (every 5 years) are critical to water pump and crossover pipe longevity. The cooling system components are the main service items - address them promptly and the engine will outlast the chassis. Many Lexus hybrid V6s have clocked 250,000+ miles on original engines with proper care. A reconditioned unit, when fitted properly, should provide another 150,000+ miles of reliable service.
